I will keep all 10.1 mu in cotton this year. That is the crop I know best after 40 years, and with only two people in the household I will keep the system simple and manageable. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on a stable cotton plan instead of taking risks with changing crops. I will use improved cotton seed because I want dependable emergence and better yield than old local seed, but I will not push inputs too hard. I will plough before planting because I want a clean seedbed and better root growth at the start of the season. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate rate of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium to support early growth, flowering, and boll setting without wasting money. Since water is available from the well, I will irrigate a few key times when cotton needs it most. I will also spray pesticides several times because insect pressure is usually a real risk in cotton, and I do not want yield loss once the season gets underway. My yield target will be steady rather than extreme, because I would rather aim for a crop I can realistically manage well.
